title: UFO Disclosure Timeline: Every Official UAP Release (1947–2026)
byline: Ivan Petricevic Published November 26, 2026 ·11 min read
excerpt: Every official UFO and UAP disclosure in one timeline: Blue Book, the CIA files, AATIP, AARO, congressional hearings and all eight 2026 Pentagon file releases, with documents.
content:
For almost 80 years, governments have investigated, denied, studied, buried and occasionally released what they know about unidentified flying objects. Since 2017 that has turned into something new: official admissions, congressional hearings, a dedicated Pentagon office and, in 2026, a rolling public release of military and intelligence files.

This page is a running record of every major official UFO and UAP disclosure: what was released, when, by whom, and where you can read the original documents yourself. It sticks to what governments actually published or said on the record. Claims made by witnesses are labeled as claims. We update it after each new release.

At a glance

  • Covers: Official US disclosures from 1947 to today, plus key releases by the UK and France.
  • Latest entry: The Pentagon’s eighth UAP file release, 20 November 2026.
  • The terms: UFO (unidentified flying object) was the official term until about 2020. UAP now means “unidentified anomalous phenomena.”
  • The bottom line so far: Many cases remain unexplained. No government has published evidence of alien technology.

Last updated: 26 November 2026.

1947–1969: The Air Force investigates

The modern UFO era began with a pilot’s report in the summer of 1947. Within months the US Air Force was formally investigating, and it kept doing so for 22 years.

  1. 24 June 1947

    Kenneth Arnold’s “flying saucers”

    Private pilot Kenneth Arnold reported nine fast, shining objects near Mount Rainier, Washington. Newspapers turned his description into “flying saucers,” and a wave of sightings followed across the United States.

  2. 8 July 1947

    Roswell: a “flying disc,” then a weather balloon

    Roswell Army Air Field in New Mexico announced it had recovered a “flying disc.” A day later, the Army said the debris came from a weather balloon. That reversal became the most famous UFO story in history. The FBI’s files from that summer include a handwritten note by J. Edgar Hoover about access to recovered discs. Read more in the Hoover note story.

  3. 23 September 1947

    The Twining memo

    Lieutenant General Nathan Twining of Air Materiel Command wrote that “the phenomenon reported is something real and not visionary or fictitious,” and recommended a formal investigation. The memo led directly to Project Sign.

  4. January 1948 – March 1952

    Projects Sign and Grudge

    The Air Force’s first official investigation, Project Sign, began in early 1948. It was replaced by Project Grudge in 1949, which took a far more dismissive approach.

  5. March 1952

    Project Blue Book begins

    The Air Force reorganized its UFO investigation as Project Blue Book. In July 1952, radar contacts and sightings over Washington, D.C., made front-page news and pushed the issue to the White House.

    National Archives: Project Blue Book records

  6. January 1953

    The CIA’s Robertson Panel

    A CIA-sponsored panel of scientists concluded that UFOs posed no direct threat. It recommended a public education campaign to reduce interest in the subject. Its role in shaping official secrecy is still debated.

    CIA: The CIA’s Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947–90

  7. January 1969

    The Condon Report

    A University of Colorado study, led by physicist Edward Condon and funded by the Air Force, concluded that further UFO research was unlikely to produce scientific discoveries. Critics noted that about 30% of the cases it studied remained unexplained.

  8. 17 December 1969

    Blue Book shuts down

    The Air Force announced the end of Project Blue Book. Over its lifetime the program logged 12,618 sightings, and 701 were never explained. The Air Force said none showed signs of a threat or of technology beyond known science. Its files are now at the US National Archives. Two years earlier, in 1967, ten nuclear missiles had gone offline at Malmstrom Air Force Base. Read what happened at Malmstrom.

    National Archives: Blue Book records

1970–2016: Freedom of Information and the archives

With Blue Book closed, almost every disclosure for the next five decades came from Freedom of Information lawsuits, leaks or foreign governments.

  1. 1978–1979

    CIA UFO documents released after a lawsuit

    A Freedom of Information Act lawsuit forced the CIA to release several hundred pages of UFO-related documents. They showed the agency had monitored the subject for decades, while saying publicly that it had no interest.

  2. 13 January 1981 (released 1983)

    The Rendlesham Forest memo

    US Air Force Lieutenant Colonel Charles Halt sent a memo to the UK Ministry of Defence describing lights and a “strange glowing object” in Rendlesham Forest, England, over several nights in December 1980. The memo was released in 1983 under the US FOIA. Rendlesham is still called “Britain’s Roswell.”

  3. 1997

    The CIA publishes its own UFO history

    CIA historian Gerald Haines published “CIA’s Role in the Study of UFOs, 1947–90.” It said many 1950s and 1960s sightings were of the CIA’s own U-2 and later SR-71 reconnaissance planes, and that the Air Force had sometimes misled the public to protect them.

    Read the CIA study (PDF)

  4. 1994–1997

    The Air Force’s Roswell reports

    After a congressional request and a General Accounting Office inquiry, the Air Force published two reports. The 1994 report said the 1947 debris came from Project Mogul, a classified program using high-altitude balloons to detect Soviet nuclear tests. The 1997 report, “The Roswell Report: Case Closed,” said accounts of “alien bodies” likely came from memories of crash-test dummies dropped in the 1950s.

  5. 2007–2012

    The secret Pentagon program

    The Defense Intelligence Agency ran the Advanced Aerospace Weapon System Applications Program (AAWSAP), which later became known as AATIP. It cost about $22 million and was not public at the time. Its existence was revealed in 2017.

  6. March 2007

    France opens its files

    France’s space agency CNES opened the archives of GEIPAN, its official UAP investigation unit, online. It became one of the first governments to publish its case files in full.

    GEIPAN case archive

  7. 2008–2013

    Britain releases its UFO desk files

    The UK National Archives released the Ministry of Defence UFO files in tranches. The last big batch was published in June 2013, after the MoD closed its UFO desk in 2009.

    UK National Archives: final tranche

2017–2022: The Pentagon admits it

In five years, the subject went from a fringe topic to an official national security issue.

  1. 16 December 2017

    The New York Times reveals AATIP

    The New York Times reported on the Pentagon’s secret UFO program and published two Navy infrared videos, including the 2004 “Tic Tac” encounter. Former official Luis Elizondo said he had resigned in protest at the secrecy. For the full story of that case, read our Tic-Tac UFO guide.

    NPR coverage

  2. 27 April 2020

    The Pentagon officially releases three Navy videos

    The Department of Defense formally released the “FLIR1,” “Gimbal” and “GoFast” videos. It said it was doing so to clear up any misconceptions about whether the footage was real, and that the objects remained “unidentified.”

    Military Times report

  3. 4 August 2020

    The UAP Task Force

    The deputy secretary of defense approved the Unidentified Aerial Phenomena Task Force, led by the Navy, to detect and analyze sightings that could threaten national security.

  4. 25 June 2021

    The first official UAP report

    The Office of the Director of National Intelligence published its Preliminary Assessment. Of 144 reports from US government sources since 2004, only one could be explained with high confidence: a deflating balloon. Eighteen incidents showed unusual movement patterns or flight characteristics.

    ODNI Preliminary Assessment (PDF)

  5. 17 May 2022

    The first public congressional UFO hearing in over 50 years

    Senior defense intelligence officials Ronald Moultrie and Scott Bray testified before a House Intelligence subcommittee and showed new videos. It was the first public hearing on the subject since the Blue Book era.

  6. June 2022 – September 2023

    NASA studies UAP

    NASA formed an independent study team in 2022. Its report, published in September 2023, found no evidence that UAP are extraterrestrial. It called for better data and an end to the stigma around reporting.

    NASA UAP study

  7. 20 July 2022

    AARO is created

    The Pentagon established the All-domain Anomaly Resolution Office (AARO) to investigate UAP across air, sea, space and underwater. It is still the government’s main UAP office today.

    AARO official site

2023–2025: Congress and the whistleblowers

Congress moved from asking questions to writing laws, and former officials began testifying under oath.

  1. 12 January 2023

    510 reports and counting

    The intelligence community’s annual report raised the total number of UAP reports to 510. Most of the newly analyzed cases were attributed to balloons, drones and clutter.

  2. 26 July 2023

    The Grusch hearing

    Former intelligence officer David Grusch told a House Oversight subcommittee that he had been informed of a decades-long program to retrieve and reverse-engineer “non-human” craft. Navy pilots David Fravor and Ryan Graves also testified. The Pentagon has denied Grusch’s claims, and he has not publicly provided evidence for them. See also what Grusch later told Joe Rogan.

    House Oversight hearing page

  3. December 2023

    A UAP records law

    Congress passed parts of the proposed UAP Disclosure Act in the 2024 defense bill (NDAA). It requires federal agencies to send their UAP records to the National Archives, which created a dedicated collection, Record Group 615.

    National Archives: UAP Records Collection

  4. 8 March 2024

    AARO’s historical report

    AARO published the first volume of its historical review. It concluded that there was no evidence any US government program had confirmed alien technology, and that many claims came from misidentified secret programs.

    AARO reports

  5. 13 November 2024

    “Exposing the Truth” hearing

    Luis Elizondo, retired Rear Admiral Tim Gallaudet, journalist Michael Shellenberger and former NASA official Michael Gold testified before the House Oversight Committee. Elizondo said the US has secret crash-retrieval programs. Read our report on the hearing.

    House Oversight hearing page

  6. 14 November 2024

    AARO’s FY2024 report: 757 new cases

    AARO reported 757 new UAP reports for May 2023 to June 2024, including a backlog of FAA reports. Twenty-one cases merited further analysis. It again found no evidence of alien technology.

  7. June 2025

    Pentagon disinformation reported

    The Wall Street Journal reported that US officials had for decades encouraged UFO stories to hide classified weapons programs. That included claims that the 1967 Malmstrom missile shutdown was linked to a secret electromagnetic pulse test.

  8. 9 September 2025

    The Hellfire video hearing

    The House Oversight task force on declassification, chaired by Representative Anna Paulina Luna, heard from military witnesses. Representative Eric Burlison showed a video of an MQ-9 drone firing a Hellfire missile at an orb off Yemen in October 2024. The missile appeared to hit the object without destroying it.

    House Oversight hearing page

2026: The files come out

In 2026 the US government began publishing UAP files directly, with new batches every few weeks at war.gov/UFO, under a program called PURSUE (Presidential Unsealing and Reporting System for UAP Encounters).

  1. 19 February 2026

    Trump orders the files released

    President Trump directed the Pentagon and other agencies to identify and release government files on UAP and extraterrestrial life, citing “tremendous interest.”

    NPR report

  2. 1 April 2026

    Congress demands 46 videos

    Representative Luna asked the Department of War to release 46 military UAP videos identified by whistleblowers, including radar, satellite and underwater encounters.

  3. 8 May 2026

    Release 1

    The first files went online, from the Pentagon, intelligence agencies, NASA and the FBI. They included federal agents’ reports of orbs over the western US in 2023, an FBI composite sketch of a bronze ellipsoid object and Apollo mission transcripts.

    AP report

  4. 22 May 2026

    Release 2: 64 files

    Fifty-one videos, seven audio files and six documents. The batch included the 2023 shootdown of an object over Lake Huron and a 2022 video of spherical objects near a submarine.

    CBS News

  5. 12 June 2026

    Release 3: 72 items

    Fifty-three documents, ten images, six videos and three NASA audio recordings. The batch included the “Orbs Over the Pond” video from October 2024.

    CBS News

  6. 10 July 2026

    Release 4: 40 files

    The batch included a 2015 Energy Department report of an unidentified object over the Pantex nuclear weapons plant in Texas.

    CBS News

  7. July 2026

    AARO’s FY2025 report: 319 new cases

    AARO received 319 new reports and resolved 370 cases in total, all with conventional explanations. Nine cases were flagged for further analysis. AARO again said it found no evidence of recovered alien material.

    AARO FY2025 report (PDF)

  8. 7 August 2026

    Release 5: 41 files

    The batch included an AC-130J gunship crew’s report of about 25 UAP during a 2021 live-fire exercise in the Gulf of Oman, which AARO could not resolve. Read what the fifth release shows.

    CBS News

  9. 18 September 2026

    Release 6: 71 files

    The batch included records from the 2008–2012 AAWSAP program and a 2010 study of three people reportedly injured after an unexplained aerospace event.

    CBS News

  10. 23 October 2026

    Release 7: 28 documents

    The batch included a June 2026 report of a silent, matte-black triangle that hovered and then left at high speed, investigated by AARO and the FBI.

    EarthSky

  11. 20 November 2026

    Release 8: 40 documents and 3 videos

    The latest batch included a 2023 civilian radar track over the western US. Read our full breakdown of the eighth release.

    war.gov/UFO

Where to read the files yourself

  • war.gov/UFO: the Pentagon’s 2026 release portal.
  • US National Archives, UAP Records Collection (RG 615).
  • Project Blue Book records at the National Archives.
  • AARO: annual reports, the historical review and resolved cases.
  • NASA’s UAP study.
  • GEIPAN: France’s official case archive.

What the record shows so far

Three things stand out from almost 80 years of disclosures. First, governments have taken the subject far more seriously than they said in public, from the 1947 Twining memo to the secret program of 2007–2012. Second, a meaningful share of reports has never been explained, from Blue Book’s 701 unidentified cases to the cases AARO still flags every year. Third, no official release has yet produced evidence of alien technology or non-human beings. The extraordinary claims come from witnesses, not from the documents.

To understand what “unidentified” really means, read why the term UAP matters, the orbs pilots keep seeing and how ufology went from fringe to mainstream.
